ActionKind.description:
The approval-gated actions this subgraph may propose.

A closed set, for the same reason `RouteDomain` is closed: a node cannot
invent a new kind of side effect, and the approval node's handling of each
kind is reviewable code rather than a generic passthrough.
ActionKind.title: ActionKind

ActionLinks.description: Where to read more about an action: its execution row and its audit trail.
ActionLinks.title: ActionLinks

ActionPreview.description:
What an outward-facing write would look like from the other side.

The part of an approval payload a reviewer reads: who receives it, under
what subject, how the body differs from what is there now, and what is
attached.
ActionPreview.title: ActionPreview

ActionReceipt.description:
What came back from redeeming one approved `ActionIntent`.

The analogue of `personalos.tools.gateway.ToolResult` at this level: it
ties an outcome back to the action it settles, so a persisted application
can record the external reference the submission returned rather than
assuming one.
ActionReceipt.title: ActionReceipt

ActionStatus.description: Where one action stands, from the outside world's point of view. Wire-visible.
ActionStatus.title: ActionStatus

ApplicationCard.description: One application as the board shows it.
ApplicationCard.title: ApplicationCard

ApplicationStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a tracked job application.

Only the states an application is allowed to occupy; which moves between
them are legal is `ALLOWED_APPLICATION_TRANSITIONS` below. Nothing writes
to `applications.status` directly — every change goes through
`validate_application_status_transition`, so an LLM-driven caller can
request a move but never set the column outright.
ApplicationStatus.title: ApplicationStatus

ApprovalDecisionInput.description:
A reviewer's answer to one `ApprovalRequest` from a pending approval.

`decided_by` is not here on purpose: it is the request's actor.
ApprovalDecisionInput.title: ApprovalDecisionInput

ApprovalOutcome.description: What a recorded decision was. Wire-visible, and written to the audit trail.
ApprovalOutcome.title: ApprovalOutcome

ArtifactSummary.description: One tailored document linked to the application. The text itself is not here.
ArtifactSummary.title: ArtifactSummary

AttachmentPreview.description: One document an action would send, identified by content rather than name.
AttachmentPreview.title: AttachmentPreview

AuditLinks.description: The rest of the chain an entry belongs to; any of them may not exist (yet).
AuditLinks.title: AuditLinks

AuditSearchResponse.description: One page of the audit trail, newest first.
AuditSearchResponse.title: AuditSearchResponse

AuditStage.description: Where in an action's life an entry sits. Declared in the order they happen.
AuditStage.title: AuditStage

AuditTrailEntry.description: One step of what happened, with the rows that explain it.
AuditTrailEntry.title: AuditTrailEntry

AuthMethod.description: How a principal was established. Recorded, never trusted for scoping.
AuthMethod.title: AuthMethod

BoardColumnView.description: One lifecycle state: this page's cards in it, and how many match in all.
BoardColumnView.title: BoardColumnView

BoardResponse.description: The board, one column per state, in lifecycle order.
BoardResponse.title: BoardResponse

CandidateProfileInput.description: What the candidate is looking for, as they state it.
CandidateProfileInput.title: CandidateProfileInput

CandidateProfileVersion.description: One stored version of an actor's profile.
CandidateProfileVersion.title: CandidateProfileVersion

CandidateProfileVersions.description: Every stored version of an actor's profile, newest first.
CandidateProfileVersions.title: CandidateProfileVersions

ChatRequest.description: Start a conversation, or continue one by naming its thread.
ChatRequest.title: ChatRequest

ChatResponse.description: What was queued: where to poll, and which thread to continue on.
ChatResponse.title: ChatResponse

CheckpointCondition.description:
The condition a pending checkpoint is re-evaluated against, stored as data.

A value rather than a callable, and that is the load-bearing choice. A
closure cannot be written to a row, cannot survive the process that built
it, and -- worse -- would capture the world as it looked when the wait
started, which is precisely the world the wait exists to let change. Storing
the *question* instead means whoever picks the checkpoint up days later asks
it fresh.

`subject_id` is what the condition is about (an application, here);
`since` bounds it in time, so "a recruiter response exists" means one that
arrived after the checkpoint was created rather than the reply from six
weeks ago that prompted it.
CheckpointCondition.title: CheckpointCondition

Commitment.description: A commitment tied to the message it was read out of.
Commitment.title: Commitment

ConditionKind.description:
What would make a pending checkpoint unnecessary.

Deliberately phrased as the *resolution* -- the thing whose existence means
"never mind" -- rather than as the reason the checkpoint was created. That
is the direction the re-evaluation asks in: at trigger time the question is
"has the thing we were waiting for happened yet?", and a `True` answer
closes the checkpoint rather than firing it.

A closed set, for the same reason `ActionKind` is closed: an evaluator has
to know how to answer every kind, and a condition nothing knows how to
evaluate is a checkpoint that either never fires or always does.
ConditionKind.title: ConditionKind

ConsentRequest.description:
A consent flow that has begun and waits for Google's redirect.

Holds nothing secret: the PKCE verifier stays in the secret store, filed
under `state`, until the redirect comes back.
ConsentRequest.title: ConsentRequest

ConstraintEffect.description: What a failed hard constraint does to the posting's score.
ConstraintEffect.title: ConstraintEffect

ConstraintResult.description: The outcome of one hard-constraint check, with the effect it carries.
ConstraintResult.title: ConstraintResult

ConstraintStatus.description: Whether a posting satisfies one of the candidate's hard constraints.
ConstraintStatus.title: ConstraintStatus

Decision.description: Outcome of evaluating an intent against policy.
Decision.title: Decision

DecisionRequest.description: A reviewer's answer to one approval.
DecisionRequest.title: DecisionRequest

DecisionResponse.description: The decision on record -- the same body for the first submission and any repeat.
DecisionResponse.title: DecisionResponse

DocumentKind.description: The formats a resume can be ingested from.
DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

EmploymentType.description: The kind of engagement a posting offers.
EmploymentType.title: EmploymentType

EventDisposition.description: Why an outbox event stopped being delivered. Wire-visible.
EventDisposition.title: EventDisposition

EventFailure.description:
An outbox event the worker gave up delivering, and what may be done about it.

Recoverable by an operator: a retry puts the event back in line with a
fresh attempt budget, for after the handler -- or, for a quarantined
event, whatever produced it -- has been fixed. Delivery is idempotent on
the event's `dedupe_key`, so a retry of an event that was in fact applied
applies nothing twice.
EventFailure.title: EventFailure

EventFailuresResponse.description: Every outbox event the worker gave up delivering, newest first.
EventFailuresResponse.title: EventFailuresResponse

EventRetryResponse.description: A parked event, back in line.
EventRetryResponse.title: EventRetryResponse

EvidenceSourceType.description:
What kind of candidate material an `evidence_chunks` row was cut from.

Distinguishes resume content from project write-ups so a retrieval query
can restrict to one kind of evidence when grounding a generated claim
(see `personalos.persistence.models.EvidenceChunkModel`).
EvidenceSourceType.title: EvidenceSourceType

FailedOperation.description: A side effect the failed step started, from its `tool_executions` row.
FailedOperation.title: FailedOperation

FailureClass.description:
Why a workflow step failed, in terms of how it may be recovered.

Wire-visible on `GET /v1/workflows/{id}/failures`. Which of these a user
may retry is `personalos.domain.failures`'s rule, not a property of the
exception: `PersonalOSError.retryable` is about *automatic* retries.
FailureClass.title: FailureClass

FailureSelection.description: Which failure to act on. Optional while the workflow has only one open.
FailureSelection.title: FailureSelection

FollowUpKind.description: Why a follow-up checkpoint was created.
FollowUpKind.title: FollowUpKind

GapSeverity.description: How much a missing requirement costs the application.
GapSeverity.title: GapSeverity

GoogleCapability.description: Something PersonalOS may do with a connected Google account. Wire-visible.
GoogleCapability.title: GoogleCapability

GoogleConnectRequest.description: Which capabilities beyond read-only to ask consent for. Empty is read-only.
GoogleConnectRequest.title: GoogleConnectRequest

GoogleConnection.description: One connected Google account, as the CLI and `GET /v1/integrations` show it.
GoogleConnection.title: GoogleConnection

GoogleRevokeRequest.description: Which account to disconnect; every connected one when absent.
GoogleRevokeRequest.title: GoogleRevokeRequest

IndexedDocument.description: A `documents` row and the evidence currently cut from it.
IndexedDocument.title: IndexedDocument

IndexedEvidence.description: One active evidence record of an ingested document.
IndexedEvidence.title: IndexedEvidence

IngestionResult.description: What one ingest of one document did.
IngestionResult.title: IngestionResult

IngestionStatus.description: What an ingest did to the index.
IngestionStatus.title: IngestionStatus

IntegrationFailuresResponse.description: Every integration that is degraded or down.
IntegrationFailuresResponse.title: IntegrationFailuresResponse

IntegrationHealth.description:
One integration's health, as its `integration_health` row records it.

Shown on a failure the integration caused, under `GET /v1/integrations`
and at `GET /v1/failures/integrations`. See `personalos.domain.health`.
IntegrationHealth.title: IntegrationHealth

IntegrationStatus.description: One integration's connection and health state, for `GET /v1/integrations`.
IntegrationStatus.title: IntegrationStatus

JobMatch.description:
The scored, explained verdict on one posting for one candidate.

`components` and `weights` are the arithmetic behind `weighted_score`;
`constraints` is what may then have lowered it to `score`. The validator
holds the two together, so a match that claims a high score past a failed
hard constraint cannot be constructed at all.
JobMatch.title: JobMatch

LinkedApproval.description: The `approvals` row an entry belongs to.
LinkedApproval.title: LinkedApproval

LinkedPolicyDecision.description: The `policy_decisions` row an entry was decided under.
LinkedPolicyDecision.title: LinkedPolicyDecision

LinkedToolExecution.description: The `tool_executions` row an entry belongs to, receipt included.
LinkedToolExecution.title: LinkedToolExecution

MatchStrength.description: How well a cited piece of evidence supports a requirement.
MatchStrength.title: MatchStrength

MatchedRequirement.description:
A posting requirement the candidate meets, and the record that proves it.

`evidence_id` is required and non-blank: a match that cites nothing is a
claim about the candidate with no source, which is exactly what gap
analysis must not produce.
MatchedRequirement.title: MatchedRequirement

MissingRequirement.description: A posting requirement nothing in the candidate's record supports.
MissingRequirement.title: MissingRequirement

OperationRecovery.description: What a retry does about one side effect of the failed step.
OperationRecovery.title: OperationRecovery

PendingApprovalItem.description: One request a reviewer is being asked to decide.
PendingApprovalItem.title: PendingApprovalItem

PendingApprovalView.description: The question a workflow is parked on.
PendingApprovalView.title: PendingApprovalView

PendingApprovalsResponse.description: The approval queue as of the last checkpoint any process wrote.
PendingApprovalsResponse.title: PendingApprovalsResponse

PendingCheckpoint.description:
One durable, conditional wait, independent of any open process.

Immutable, like every other value crossing a layer here: a sweeper that
could mutate the checkpoint it is deciding about could decide against a
checkpoint different from the one it then records. Closing one produces a
new value (`closed_as`), and the store's guarded `UPDATE` is what makes that
close exclusive between two sweepers.

The three fields that make this survivable are `condition`, `trigger_at`
and `expires_at`, and they are independent on purpose -- see the module
docstring. `thread_id` (with `workflow_id`) is how the checkpoint names the
graph path to start when it fires: a *lookup key*, resolved by
`personalos.persistence.checkpointer.WorkflowThreadRegistry` at trigger
time, never a live handle.
PendingCheckpoint.title: PendingCheckpoint

PendingCheckpointStatus.description:
Where a pending checkpoint is in its life.

Four terminal states rather than one, because "why did this never fire?" is
the question an operator actually asks, and collapsing them into `closed`
would throw away the answer.
PendingCheckpointStatus.title: PendingCheckpointStatus

Recommendation.description: What the run advises doing with one posting.
Recommendation.title: Recommendation

RecoverableFailureView.description: A node failure whose checkpoint is intact, so a resume can retry it.
RecoverableFailureView.title: RecoverableFailureView

RecoveryAction.description: What a user is offered for a failure.
RecoveryAction.title: RecoveryAction

RecruiterEventSummary.description: One recruiter-side signal recorded against the application.
RecruiterEventSummary.title: RecruiterEventSummary

RefusalReason.description:
Why an approved-looking action was not executed after all.

A closed set so a refusal is classifiable rather than a string an operator
has to read: `HASH_MISMATCH` and `EXPIRED` mean something went wrong
between the request and the resume and want investigating, while
`DENIED_BY_USER` is the ordinary outcome of a reviewer saying no.
RefusalReason.title: RefusalReason

ResumeRequest.description:
The answer to whatever the workflow is waiting on.

Exactly one of `decisions` (for an approval) or `event` (for anything else
an interrupt waits on) must be given.
ResumeRequest.title: ResumeRequest

ResumeResponse.description: What was queued in answer to the interrupt.
ResumeResponse.title: ResumeResponse

RetryResponse.description: What was queued, and what the re-run will do about each side effect.
RetryResponse.title: RetryResponse

SeniorityLevel.description:
Career level of a role, in ascending order.

Ordered so "how far is this posting from what the candidate wants" is a
subtraction (see `rank`) rather than a table of pairs.
SeniorityLevel.title: SeniorityLevel

ShortlistItem.description: One posting a run recommended, and whether anything was done about it.
ShortlistItem.title: ShortlistItem

StepView.description: One graph node, on the thread it belongs to.
StepView.title: StepView

StreamTicketRequest.description: Which workflow's event stream the ticket opens.
StreamTicketRequest.title: StreamTicketRequest

StreamTicketResponse.description: A ticket, when it expires, and the URL to open with it.
StreamTicketResponse.title: StreamTicketResponse

TailoringSuggestion.description:
One way to present the candidate's existing record for this posting.

`evidence_id` is optional because some advice is about a gap ("address the
missing Go experience up front") rather than about a record. When it is
set it must resolve, like any other citation.
TailoringSuggestion.title: TailoringSuggestion

TransitionEffect.description:
Something outside this system a manual transition asks to have done.

A closed set, like `ActionKind`, and each member maps onto exactly one of
those kinds: a transition cannot invent a side effect the graph has no
reviewed handling for.
TransitionEffect.title: TransitionEffect

TransitionRequest.description: A status change, and optionally something to do outside the system with it.
TransitionRequest.title: TransitionRequest

TransitionResponse.description: The answer to a move: the card as it now stands, and what happened.
TransitionResponse.title: TransitionResponse

WorkMode.description: Where the candidate is willing to do the work.
WorkMode.title: WorkMode

WorkflowAction.description:
One outward-facing action, labelled with what actually became of it.

The shape every surface lists an action in. `action_status` is required --
there is no default -- so an action object that does not say whether it
happened is not a valid one.
WorkflowAction.title: WorkflowAction

WorkflowFailure.description: One failed step of a workflow, and what may be done about it.
WorkflowFailure.title: WorkflowFailure

WorkflowStatus.description:
Where one workflow stands, across all of its threads.

Wire-visible: a client matches on these strings.
WorkflowStatus.title: WorkflowStatus

WorkflowStatusResponse.description:
Where a workflow stands, as of the last row any process wrote.

`actions` is what was suggested and what was done, in one list: each item's
`action_status` says which. Only `EXECUTED` means something happened
outside this system, and every `EXECUTED` item carries its receipt and its
audit links. `pending_approval` is the raw interrupt, kept for the resume
endpoint; read the `AWAITING_APPROVAL` actions for what it asks.
WorkflowStatusResponse.title: WorkflowStatusResponse

HTTPBearer.description: The local API token: `python -m personalos.cli auth token`.

get.description: Liveness: 200 while the API process can serve a request.

The board: applications grouped by lifecycle state, a page at a time.

`state` may be repeated to show several columns. Pages run through the
board in column order, most recently active first within a column.
One application: fit, evidence, documents, recruiter events and open waits.

post.description:
Move an application to another lifecycle state.

An illegal move is a 422 whose body lists `allowed_next_states`. A move
with no `effect` is applied at once (200). A move with an `effect` is
put to the policy engine -- a denial is a 403 -- and otherwise queued for
approval (202); a second one while the first is still in flight is a 409.

get.description: Every approval still owed an answer, oldest first; expired ones are marked.

post.description:
Approve or reject one pending approval.

Approving resumes the workflow through the worker; rejecting records
`DENIED_BY_USER` and resumes it down its declined branch. A mismatched
`action_hash`, approving an expired approval, and reversing a recorded
decision are each a 409. Repeating a recorded decision returns it
unchanged and resumes nothing a second time.

get.description:
Audit events matching every filter given, newest first.

`application_id` matches the workflows run on that application's own
thread -- the board moves made on it. `since` and `until` are inclusive.

post.description: A short-lived ticket for one workflow's event stream.

get.description: The actor this caller's credential verified as.

post.description:
Start a Supervisor conversation, or continue one, by queuing a run of it.

Continuing a conversation whose workflow is parked on an approval is a
409: a new message would start the thread over and strand the question it
is waiting on. Answer it through the resume endpoint first.
Ingest the resume at `path` as the actor's evidence.

get.description: Every dead-lettered or quarantined event, with its last error, newest first.

post.description:
Put a dead-lettered or quarantined event back in line, with a fresh attempt budget.

A 404 when there is no such event, and a 409 when it is not parked --
pending, being delivered, or delivered.

get.description: Every degraded or down integration, with its reason and what fixes it.
Every integration's connection and health state. Never includes token material.
Google's redirect: finish the consent and store the refresh token.

post.description: Begin Google consent; open the returned `authorization_url` in a browser.
Revoke at Google and delete the keychain entry.

get.description: The actor's latest profile version -- the one a job search loads.

post.description: Write the first version of the actor's profile.

put.description: Write the next version of the actor's profile; earlier versions stay as they were.

get.description: Every version of the actor's profile, newest first.
One numbered version of the actor's profile.
Plan, completed steps, labelled actions, pending approval, failures, audit link.
Everything recorded for one workflow, in the order it happened.

post.description:
Acknowledge a failure and close it, without retrying it.

Nothing is re-run and nothing is undone: the step stays failed, and the
dismissal is an audit event naming who closed it. A 409 for a failure
already dismissed, or one with a retry queued -- let the retry finish.

get.description:
Stream the workflow's progress events, resuming after `Last-Event-ID` if given.

The header wins over `?last_event_id=` when both are sent: it is what a
reconnecting `EventSource` sets, and it is the newer of the two.
Every failed step, with its class, whether it can be retried, and why not.

post.description:
Queue the answer to the interrupt a workflow is parked on.

A workflow that is not parked on anything -- still queued, running,
finished, or already answered and waiting for the worker -- is a 409
naming its actual status, never a silently accepted no-op. So is an answer
racing another answer to the same interrupt: the queue refuses the second.

Queue a re-run of a failed step, from the checkpoint before it.

A 409 when the failure is not retryable -- a policy denial, a provider
that needs reconnecting, a step out of attempts, one already dismissed or
already being retried -- naming the reason.
